# PZEMU — Games and cartridges

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_games_md.py from PZEMU_Distributions.lua. Do not edit by hand. -->

PZEMU ships **no commercial ROMs**. Every game below is a *cartridge item* that can spawn in
loot; to actually play it you must supply your own legally obtained ROM dump and drop it in
the matching folder under `Zomboid/PZEMU/roms/` (see the last section). The three bundled
free homebrew NES games are marked **bundled** and work out of the box.

Columns: **ROM file** is the name PZEMU looks for first (exact), then it falls back to fuzzy
matching. **Item** says whether the game has its own cartridge item with a dedicated icon,
or spawns as the system's generic cartridge with the game name written on it.
**Weight** is the relative spawn weight inside that system's pool (higher = more common);
**Share** is weight / pool total. The first entry of every pool is the *must-have* game
that always spawns next to a console (unless the Cartridge Count Multiplier is 0).

- [NES (Nintendo Entertainment System)](#nes-nintendo-entertainment-system) — 61 games, folder `roms/nes/`

## How to add your own games and cartridges

### 1. Where ROMs go

`<Zomboid user folder>/PZEMU/roms/<system>/` where `<system>` is one of `nes`, `snes`, `genesis`, `gb`, `atari2600`, `gg`, `sms`.

- Linux: `~/Zomboid/PZEMU/roms/nes/`
- Windows: `C:\Users\<you>\Zomboid\PZEMU\roms\nes\`

The folders are created the first time the emulator runs; you can also create them yourself.
Only the extensions listed per system above are considered. Zipped ROMs are not read.

### 2. How ROM names are matched

When you pick a game, PZEMU looks for the exact **ROM file** name first. If it is not there,
every file in the system folder (with a matching extension) is normalised and compared:

1. the extension is removed;
2. everything from the first `(` or `[` onwards is dropped — region, revision and dump tags
   such as `(USA)`, `(Rev A)`, `(PRG1)`, `[!]`;
3. apostrophes (straight and curly), commas and periods are removed;
4. hyphens, en/em dashes and colons become `_`; runs of spaces/underscores collapse to one `_`;
5. the result is lower-cased and common accents are stripped (Pokémon → pokemon);
6. a leading `The`/`A`/`An` and a trailing `, The`/`, A`/`, An` are dropped;
7. roman numerals II–X become 2–10 (`Final Fantasy III` → `final_fantasy_3`).

The two normalised names must then be **identical** (there is no prefix or similarity matching,
so `Dragon Warrior` never matches `Dragon Warrior II`). Examples that all resolve to
`Super_Mario_Bros_3.nes`: `Super Mario Bros. 3 (USA) (PRG1) [!].nes`, `super-mario-bros-iii.nes`,
`Super_Mario_Bros_3.NES`.

If a game cannot be found, the emulator window shows the expected file name and the folder.

### 3. Adding a game to a loot pool

Open `mod/PZEMU/42/media/lua/server/Items/PZEMU_Distributions.lua` and add one line to the
system's `*_GAME_POOL` table (anywhere after the first entry — the first entry is the must-have game):

```lua
    { name = "Bubble Bobble 2",  romFile = "Bubble_Bobble_2.nes",  namedItem = nil,  weight = 5 },
```

- `name` — what the cartridge is called in the inventory (the system prefix `NES: ` is added
  automatically) and in the game picker.
- `romFile` — the file name PZEMU expects in `roms/<system>/` (use `_` instead of spaces; the
  fuzzy matcher handles most other spellings).
- `namedItem = nil` — spawn as the generic cartridge of that system with the name stamped on it.
- `weight` — relative spawn weight within the pool; 50 is "everyone had this", 1–3 is rare.

Cartridges only spawn next to a console of the same system (3–7 per console, 15% chance of a
bigger stash, scaled by the *Cartridge Count Multiplier* sandbox option). Changes to the pool apply
to containers that have not been opened yet; already-generated loot is unaffected. Spawning is
server-side: in multiplayer the server's copy of the file is what counts.

### 4. Giving a game its own cartridge item (icon)

Three edits:

1. `mod/PZEMU/42/media/scripts/pzemu_items.txt` — add an item in module `PZEMU`:

```
    item NES_Cart_BubbleBobble2
    {
        ItemType            = base:normal,
        DisplayName         = NES: Bubble Bobble 2,
        Weight              = 0.1,
        Icon                = PZEMU_NES_Cart_BubbleBobble2,
        DisplayCategory     = Electronics,
        Tags                = PZEMU_Cartridge;PZEMU_NES,
        WorldStaticModel    = PZEMU_NES_Cart_Generic,
    }
```

   and put a 32×32 (or larger, square) PNG at `mod/PZEMU/42/media/textures/Item_PZEMU_NES_Cart_BubbleBobble2.png`.
2. `PZEMU_Distributions.lua` — set `namedItem = "PZEMU.NES_Cart_BubbleBobble2"` on the pool entry.
3. `mod/PZEMU/42/media/lua/client/PZEMU/PZEMUMain.lua` — add the item to both lookup tables:
   `CART_TYPE_TO_SYSTEM["PZEMU.NES_Cart_BubbleBobble2"] = "nes"` and
   `NAMED_CART_ROMS["PZEMU.NES_Cart_BubbleBobble2"] = "Bubble_Bobble_2.nes"`.

Re-run `python3 tools/gen_games_md.py` afterwards to refresh this file; it warns (⚠) when the
ROM file in `PZEMUMain.lua` disagrees with the pool.

### 5. Adding a whole new system

Not supported by drop-in configuration: a new system needs a libretro core shipped as `.dat`,
a `CONSOLES` entry in `PZEMUGame.lua` (resolution, core file, button list, key map), console and
cartridge items, lookup tables in `PZEMUMain.lua` and a pool here. See `analog.md` in the repo
for the advanced-user walkthrough that adds PSX/PSP cores.
